rv.q: Yet it’s a baggy old evening, not quite a full-on gagfest, but too broad to sustain its aspirations to be something more substantial.

Mischief may well be swerving into becoming natural successors to Alan Ayckbourn, at one time a stalwart brand of West End comedy, but structurally the tone isn't, as yet, as confident, deft or outright funny.

cn.t: Mischief Theatre's comedy about childhood friendships receives a lukewarm reception, with critics finding the tone less confident and the humor less sharp than the company's previous hits.
